clue.text: Bloomer crudely put could be such, if accepted

indicators.note: something put crudely is roughly rearranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: Someone excuses a blunder, saying a crudely phrased remark could pass if people accepted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is literally a thing that blooms: a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuchsia is a flowering shrub, and anything that flowers can jokingly be called a bloomer.

clue.text: ____ is frequently behind the sign of woodworm, eg

parts.note: FR is a dictionary abbreviation for frequently
a behind is the backside, the American ass

explanation.surface: The blank-led sentence reads as if something is often found behind a telltale woodworm hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank stands for the answer itself, so the clue reads 'the answer is ... the sign of woodworm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frass is the powdery wood debris and droppings that boring insects leave, the visible evidence of woodworm.

clue.text: Seat of learning on norm not now directly made in one piece

parts.note: short for university
par is the norm or standard; 'on' places it after the first piece
tite is an obsolete word meaning promptly or directly; 'not now' marks it as archaic

explanation.surface: A university is said to sit on a norm that is no longer applied directly to things built whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not now' flags an obsolete word, a common Mephisto convention for drawing on Chambers' archaic entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Unipartite means consisting of a single part, i.e. not divided into separate sections.

clue.text: Buzz about gold anemone's tip — marine building blocks?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is to phone, or call, them
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its starting end, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the anemone

explanation.surface: A query about whether a sea anemone's golden tip contributes to building reefs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anemone suggests the sea creature, but it supplies one letter; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coralla are the hard skeletons of coral colonies, the units from which reefs are built up underwater.

clue.text: Couple from Hebron holding up stiff letter of theirs?

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece holding up another sits above it, so this order is fixed

parts.note: sad is used of bread or cake that is heavy and stiff, having failed to rise

indicators.note: a couple is two, so only the opening pair of letters is taken

parts.note: the first two letters of Hebron

explanation.surface: Someone picks two people from Hebron, who prop up a formal letter from them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theirs' points back to Hebron, a city in the Hebrew-speaking world, so the letter is one of the Hebrew alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadhe is the eighteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, belonging to the people of Hebron's language.

clue.text: Colouring decorative dot but black stuck

indicators.note: but here means except, so the named letter is excluded

parts.note: a bindi is the decorative dot worn on the forehead in South Asia
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
stuck with horns, as by a bull

explanation.surface: A painted decorative dot, with black paint stuck on, gives some colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' reads as a conjunction; it means 'without', removing B from the dot.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo red is a reddish dye obtained from indigo, so it is a colouring matter.

clue.text: Old tapestry frames where padres preach

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete word for the frames on which tapestry was stretched
second meaning: canvas shelters used for revival meetings and field services

explanation.walkthrough: Army padres and evangelists have long preached under canvas, as in American tent revivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the old frames for stretching tapestry and the canvas shelters used for open-air preaching.

clue.text: Eg, Trinity's empty when 3rd is close to poor

indicators.note: the third letter is swapped out and something else put in its place

parts.note: to teem is an old sense meaning to empty or pour out

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of poor

explanation.surface: An Oxford college's Trinity seems deserted when its third-year students are near poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity is not a college here but the summer term at Oxford and some other universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is the name of the summer academic period at Oxford, so it is an example of a university term.

clue.text: Rising self-importance and breach in reasoning

indicators.note: in a down entry something rising runs from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: an inflated ego is self-importance
a gape is an opening or breach

explanation.surface: Swelling conceit causes a break in someone's logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Epagoge is Aristotle's term for inductive reasoning, arguing from particular cases to a general rule.

clue.text: Geese spotted heading northwards around noon

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means going upwards, so the word is read backwards
around means surrounding, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: spotted means seen
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers report geese seen flying north around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Nenes are Hawaiian geese, a species of goose native to Hawaii.

clue.text: Series about advanced trick used by Ned Kelly and his ilk

definitions.text: trick used by Ned Kelly and his ilk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the second piece is placed within the first

parts.note: SER is an abbreviation for series
advanced, as of money, means lent

explanation.surface: A run of stories about some upfront dodge pulled by Australian bushrangers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a notorious 19th-century Australian outlaw, pointing to Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slenter is Australian slang for a trick or swindle, the kind of dodge an outlaw would pull.

clue.text: Oscar called Steed's sidekick, I suppose, sugar-coated candy?

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
rang means telephoned, called
Emma Peel was John Steed's partner in the TV series The Avengers; 'I suppose' hedges the shortened form, initial plus surname, E. Peel

explanation.surface: An awards recipient phones about a TV spy's partner, who seems to be a sweet-talker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avengers was a 1960s British spy series in which Diana Rigg played Emma Peel opposite John Steed.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied orange rind is a confection, so orange peel coated in sugar counts as a sweet; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: That which winds Guevara up in revolutionary broadcast

indicators.note: what winds a word up is the thing that finishes it, its final letter
completes 'winds up', meaning brings to an end, so the closing letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Guevara
I is a dictionary abbreviation for in
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Something that riles Che Guevara turns up in a revolutionary radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds up' suggests annoying Che, but it means finishes: the letter that ends his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme or opinion is to broadcast it, so aired is the past participle synonym.

clue.text: Discarded porridge managed to be consumed by leader

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title
managed, as a business, means ran

explanation.surface: A leader manages to eat porridge that others threw away.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for time served in prison, not the breakfast; 'Discarded' marks the answer as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Durance is an archaic word for imprisonment, the same thing as porridge in British slang.

clue.text: Cold murder arranged with a certain instrument

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a hit is a contract killing
ARR is the abbreviation for arranged, as in musical credits
'a certain' person is 'one' person, as in 'one Mr Smith'

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded killing is plotted, with some particular instrument as the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but it is just the abbreviation ARR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chitarrone is a large bass lute of the early Baroque, a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Plated silver's left with chap, it must be restored

indicators.note: the left end of a word is where it starts, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of silver

indicators.note: restoring something rebuilds it, so these letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some plated silverware is left with a man, who has to get it repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plated' suggests silver plate, but it describes a mineral that splits into thin layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Spathic describes spar-like minerals that are lamellar, made of thin flat layers or plates.

clue.text: Clip vehicle, a black one, narrowly missing American

indicators.note: something missing is left out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
I is the Roman numeral one
near as an adverb, as in a near-run thing, means narrowly
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A vehicle clips a black one, narrowly missing an American pedestrian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' reads as a verb for striking a car, but it is a noun naming the climbing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabiner is a metal spring-gated clip used by climbers to attach ropes.

clue.text: A form of willow selling in northern town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dialect name for the sallow, a kind of willow
second meaning: the act of selling something
third meaning: a town in Greater Manchester in the north of England

explanation.surface: Willow is being sold off in some town in the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: This has three definitions rather than two; Sale is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a willow variety, the act of disposing of goods for money, and an English town.

clue.text: Scot on the fiddle uses this run out to brood

definitions.text: Scot on the fiddle uses this

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
a hen sits on her brood, so to brood is to sit

explanation.surface: A Scottish swindler, running out of time, is left to sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' suggests cheating, but it means playing the violin; rosit is the Scots form of rosin, applied to bows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler rubs rosin on the bow for grip, and rosit is the Scots dialect word for that resin.

clue.text: Dance display features little variety for old admiral

indicators.note: something that features an item contains it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nach is a display of Indian dancing
VAR is the short form of variety

explanation.surface: A dance show offers little variety, suiting a retired naval officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A navarch was the commander of a fleet in ancient Greece, the equivalent of an admiral.

clue.text: Fantastic, give a Tory opening for false dreams

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly imaginative, so these letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at handing a Conservative the chance to peddle illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer and Virgil, true dreams come through a gate of horn and false ones through a gate of ivory.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth the ivory gate is the portal through which deceptive dreams pass to sleepers.

clue.text: Interest over region's means

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for interest
an end is a region or district, as in West End; with the 's, END'S
in a down entry this places the first piece above the next

explanation.surface: A financial note: the interest paid exceeds a district's available funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a noun for money, but it is the verb, as in 'she means to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, so 'means' and 'intends' are interchangeable verbs.

clue.text: Blast, la vache! Better to split losses ____

indicators.note: a blast scatters things, so the letters land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written; French for 'the cow'

explanation.surface: A frustrated French gambler curses the cow, then advises hedging bets to limit losses.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the answer; a better, i.e. one who bets, places a stake straddling two numbers to split the risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheval is a gambling term for a stake divided between two adjacent numbers or chances, as in roulette.

clue.text: Whatever may happen advance and beat your goddess

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advance
to tan someone's hide is to beat them
YR is the abbreviation for your
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A warrior vows to press on and defeat your goddess come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'in any case' or 'regardless', the same sense as whatever may happen.

clue.text: It's in pass, it's something to take in

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a visa is a pass permitting entry to a country
'T is the old contracted form of it, as in 'tis and 'twas

explanation.surface: A mountain pass, it turns out, is something you simply have to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests a mountain route, fitting the scenery, but it is an entry permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a broad view, and to take in a view is to look at and absorb it.

clue.text: Bawd mostly admitted to it? It gets you hot and steamy

definitions.text: It gets you hot and steamy

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so it goes into the other piece

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: aunt is an old slang word for a bawd or procuress

explanation.surface: A madam half-confesses to sex appeal, and finds herself in a hot, steamy place.
explanation.walkthrough: The suggestive surface leads to a bathhouse; 'it' as sex appeal comes from the 1927 film It starring Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a heated room filled with steam or dry heat, which makes you hot and sweaty.

clue.text: Special number to ring on a tablet

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A special number to call is printed on a tablet computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests a device or a pill, but it is an inscribed slab of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright stone slab bearing an inscription, a tablet in the ancient sense.

clue.text: Share international title

parts.note: SHR is a dictionary abbreviation for share
I is an abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A shared international title, as if a trophy were jointly held.
explanation.definitionFit: Shri is an Indian honorific, a respectful title placed before a man's name.

clue.text: One year skate over twenty-nine spring days

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Y is an abbreviation for year

indicators.note: turned over means upended, so in a down entry the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: the skate is a kind of ray

explanation.surface: Someone spends a year skating through a month of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skate' looks like a verb but is the flat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Iyyar is a month of the Jewish calendar falling in April-May, and it always has twenty-nine days.

clue.text: Bird that chatters to Scot, mine involves English

indicators.note: something that involves another takes it within itself, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Scottish miner talks to a chattering bird while working in an English pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To Scot' means as far as a Scot is concerned: the answer is a Scots dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Piet is the Scots name for the magpie, a bird famous for its chattering call.

clue.text: Italian understood male in unsympathetic Havering

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another

parts.note: dry means cold and unsympathetic
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
he is the pronoun understood to refer to a male

explanation.surface: An Italian man was understood to be unsympathetic in the London borough of Havering.
explanation.walkthrough: Havering is a London borough, but here it is the Scots and British word for dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is to hesitate or vacillate, so havering describes the same indecisive state as dithery.

clue.text: Concerning one in French isle just after gathering for friends?

parts.note: re means concerning
un is French for one
I is the abbreviation for isle
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A notice about a French island holding a get-together for old friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French isle' strongly evokes Réunion in the Indian Ocean, which helpfully is also the answer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion is a meeting of people, such as old friends or classmates, who have been apart.

clue.text: Resent involving old diplomat who's second-rate

indicators.note: something involving another takes it within itself, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to envy is to resent another's good fortune
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone resents an old diplomat who never quite made the grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-rate' sounds like a sneer, but it is literal: this diplomat ranks just below an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a diplomatic minister of the second rank, below an ambassador in protocol order.

clue.text: Pick-me-up adding energy all over mushroom?

parts.note: a cinder is a dialect term for a dash of spirits added to another drink as a pick-me-up
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tonic that boosts energy everywhere seems to be some kind of magic mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: A mushroom is also an upstart who springs up suddenly from obscurity, like the fairy-tale heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella rose from scullery to princess overnight, just as a mushroom, an upstart, rises suddenly; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Spenser's vow is in trouble

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: heat is pressure or trouble, as in 'the heat is on'
'S is the contracted form of is

explanation.surface: The poet Spenser's promise has landed him in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Spenser, the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene, flags an archaic spelling he used.
explanation.definitionFit: Heast is Spenser's form of hest, an old word for a command or solemn promise.

clue.text: Brother passes round something for boring fighter

indicators.note: passing round something means encircling it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Brer is the dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit
an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A sibling hands round a tool to a dull boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests tedious, making a dull fighter; it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawler is someone who fights noisily and roughly, a street fighter.
